T: New York welcome. Hong Kong kicks.
D: A Hong Kong cop visiting his uncle in New York ends up protecting a supermarket from a street gang.
P: Serve the mains at his uncle's wedding banquet.
S: the family supermarket everyone is fighting over

Rye bread squares stacked with pastrami, sauerkraut and Swiss, toasted until the cheese melts, with a dab of Russian dressing and a pickle on a pick. Cut 6 slices of rye bread into quarters and toast lightly at 200C for 4 minutes. Top each with folded pastrami from 250g, a little drained sauerkraut from 150g and a square of Swiss cheese from 150g. Bake 5 minutes until melted. Mix 4 tbsp mayonnaise with 1 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp horseradish and chopped pickle. Dab on each bite and spear with a slice of dill pickle.
his uncle's Chinese family in New York
Pork, garlic chives, ginger and sesame oil folded into wrappers, pan-fried until crisp underneath, then steamed. Black vinegar dip.
Uncle Bill's family in New York

Soft steamed buns filled with sticky honey and hoisin barbecue pork, steamed until puffed and served hot with extra hoisin for dipping. Dice 300g char siu pork and stir into 2 tbsp hoisin, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp oyster sauce and 80ml water thickened with 1 tsp cornflour. Cool. Mix 300g bao flour, 5g dried yeast, 30g sugar and 160ml warm water, knead 8 minutes and prove 1 hour. Divide into 12, roll into discs, fill and pleat closed. Prove 20 minutes on squares of baking paper and steam 12 minutes. Serve with hoisin.
M: Ginger and spring onion lobster noodles

Lobster tails cut through the shell and wok-fried with ginger and spring onion in a light oyster sauce, piled over crisp-edged soft egg noodles. Cut 4 lobster tails through the shell into chunks, or use 800g king prawns. Dust in cornflour and fry in a hot wok for 2 minutes, then set aside. Pan-fry 400g boiled egg noodles in oil until crisp underneath. Stir-fry 50g sliced ginger and 6 spring onion lengths, add the lobster, 2 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine and 150ml chicken stock and toss 2 minutes. Pour over the noodles.
Pork shoulder pieces in a light batter, fried crisp, tossed in a sauce of pineapple, capsicum, vinegar, sugar and tomato sauce. Steamed rice.
W: Milk set with gelatine and almond extract, cut into cubes, served with lychees and mandarin segments in syrup.
K: Fragrant jasmine tea steeped strong, sweetened with lychee syrup, poured over ice with whole lychees and a twist of lime. Heat 1L water to just off the boil and steep 5 tsp jasmine tea for 4 minutes, then strain and cool. Drain a 565g tin of lychees, keeping the syrup. Stir 150ml of the syrup and the juice of a lime into the tea and chill for an hour. Fill four tall glasses with ice and a few lychees, pour in the tea and finish with a twist of lime peel.

s.how: Mix 400g pork mince with a chopped bunch of garlic chives, 1 tbsp grated ginger and 1 tsp sesame oil. Fill 30 dumpling wrappers and pleat. Fry until crisp underneath, add water and steam under a lid for 4 minutes. Serve with black vinegar.

m.how: Toss 700g diced pork shoulder in egg and 100g cornflour and fry at 180C until crisp. Simmer chunks of half a pineapple and a red capsicum with 80ml vinegar, 80g sugar and 80ml tomato sauce, then thicken. Toss the pork through and serve with 300g jasmine rice.

w.how: Soak 4 gelatine leaves. Warm 500ml milk with 60g sugar, stir in the gelatine and 1 tsp almond extract. Set in a tray for 3 hours and cut into cubes. Serve in bowls with a tin of lychees and mandarin segments in their syrup.
